page: Amazon Web Services r6id.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors. It features 128 virtual CPUs across 64 physical cores with a base clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is provided by 7600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

In performance evaluations, the r6id.metal demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, highlighted by a top-tier Passmark CPU score of 88,191.68 and a strong stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 124,966.04. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 338.87 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 132.33 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Database operations are also a strength, with Passmark database operations scoring 30,511.07 and Redis SET operations reaching 110.69 million operations per second. Single-core performance, however, is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1,908.5 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,670.0, indicating that workloads relying heavily on single-threaded execution may not fully leverage this hardware class.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r6id.metal offers high resource density by combining a large 1 TB memory footprint with high-capacity, low-latency local NVMe storage on a dedicated bare-metal platform. This eliminates virtualization overhead and makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive, data-heavy workloads. Appropriate workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, extensive database operations, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
